name: GATE-style
fullName: Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (any paper)

coverage.note: Marks, duration and marking verified from the GATE 2025 question paper pattern page (IIT Roorkee): 100 marks, 3 hours, General Aptitude 15 marks, questions of 1 or 2 marks, −1/3 and −2/3 for wrong MCQs, no negative and no partial marks for MSQ and NAT. The section split below is NOT official: the counts of MCQ/MSQ/NAT vary by paper and year and are an assumption for practice. Verified 29 Oct 2026 against the cited sources.

sections.name: Subject – MSQ
sections.style: one or more correct; no partial credit, no negative

sections.name: Subject – NAT 1 mark
sections.style: numerical answer within a stated range

sections.name: Subject – NAT 2 marks
sections.style: numerical answer within a stated range

pattern.notes: 65 questions, 100 marks: General Aptitude 15 marks, subject 85 marks. MCQ wrong answers lose 1/3 (1-mark) or 2/3 (2-mark). The exact MCQ/MSQ/NAT counts here are an assumed typical split.

notes: Engineering-maths and core-subject application problems; NAT questions need exact numerical work.
General Aptitude: verbal and quantitative reasoning.

traps: NAT answers must fall inside the accepted range (watch rounding).
MSQ gives zero unless every correct option and no wrong one is chosen.
Negative marking only on MCQs — never on MSQ or NAT.
assumptions: GA as 5 one-mark + 5 two-mark MCQs and the subject split (20+15 MCQ, 5 MSQ, 5+10 NAT) are assumed; GATE does not fix them.
Difficulty and topic weights are unknown (vary by paper), so the generic mix is used.
